newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Q1 GDP rises 2.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Q1 GDP rises 2.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Dutch first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) rose a provisional 2.1 percent year-on-year, the Central Bureau of Statistics (CBS) said.
The CBS said that after stripping out calendar effects, it estimated that first quarter GDP had grown at an underlying year-on-year rate of 3.0 percent.
NOTE - Figures show real percent changes and are not adjusted for calendar effects.
The CBS said a "leap-year effect" had held back the headline rate of Dutch economic growth in the first quarter of 1997 to a year-on-year rate of 2.1 percent.
But figures adjusted to eliminate the effect of the extra day in February 1996 showed that Gross Domestic Product (GDP) grew at an underlying year-on-year rate of about 3.0 percent.
The CBS noted that this was in line with the pace of Dutch GDP growth in the second half of 1996.
Economists polled by Reuters had expected Dutch first quarter GDP to show a year-on-year rise of 3.0 percent.
